question.problem: The eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -8+k \\ 3 & 5k\end{aligned}]$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2k$ is  $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -8+k \\ 3 & 5k\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =2k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}k-10 \\ -6+5k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4k \\ 2k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}k-10=-4k, \\ -6+5k=2k\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $k$ in the first equation, we get

$$
k-10=-4k\,⟹\,k=2.
$$

Now, substituting $k=2$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-6+5k & =2k \\ -6+5(2) & =2(2) \\ 4 & =4,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a true statement.

Therefore, the solution of the system is $k=2.$
